subject: biology

items.q: Which way do arrows point in a food chain?
items.correct: From prey to predator, showing the direction of energy flow.
items.misconception: From predator to prey, because predators eat prey.
items.why: The arrow follows the energy: it is transferred from the organism eaten to the one eating it.

items.q: Is energy recycled in an ecosystem?
items.correct: No — energy flows through and is lost as heat; only nutrients are recycled.
items.misconception: Yes, the same energy goes round and round forever.
items.why: At each level energy is lost (mostly as heat in respiration), so it must be constantly resupplied by the Sun.

items.correct: They recycle nutrients from dead matter back into the ecosystem.
items.misconception: They are not important and could be removed.
items.random_wrong: They produce all the oxygen on Earth.
items.why: Without decomposers, nutrients would stay locked in dead organisms and not return to the soil.

items.q: What happens if a predator is removed from a food web?
items.correct: Prey populations can rise and the whole web is disrupted.
items.why: Food webs are interconnected, so removing one species has knock-on effects throughout.
